To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Mmm1p, an integral mitochondrial membrane protein, spans both mitochondrial membranes, exposing a large N-terminal extension to the matrix, 2) this matrix-exposed N-terminal domain is not essential for mitochondrial morphology, and 3) the C-terminal domain is required for mitochondrial targeting, whereas the transmembrane domain is necessary for foci formation.
the matrix-exposure of Mmm1 is not essential for mitochondrial foci formation and that the transmemembrane segment is required for mitochondrial foci maintenance.
the integral membrane protein, Mmm1p, is required for maintenance and organization of mitochondrial DNA and is a key component of the membrane contact site in mitochondria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the Mmm complex.
the role of Mmm1 in mitochondrial morphology and mtDNA maintenance.
the molecular mechanism of Mmm1-mediated mitochondrial foci formation and its function in mitochondrial morphology and mtDNA maintenance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the double membrane spanning topology of Mmm is required for formation of tubule mitochondria and that the matrix exposed N-terminus is required to stabilize the protein.
Mmm1 is an essential protein that is required for the maintenance of mitochondrial structure and function.
the N-terminal domain of Mm1p is not required for the function of the protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mmm1p foci are not essential for mt DNA nucleoid maintenance, but the double membrane spanning topology is essential for formation of tubules.
Mmm1 protein is a double-membrane spanning protein, with its C termini facing to the cytoplasm and its N termini exposed to the mitochondrial matrix.
Mmm1 protein is a key factor in the formation and maintenance of tubular mitochondrion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Mmm1 is a mitochondrial membrane protein that is required for the maintenance of the mitochondrial network.
the N terminus of the Mmm protein is not required for its function, but rather that the transmembranespanning domain is required to maintain mitochondrial morphology.
Mmm1 is a mitochondrial protein that spans both the outer mitochondrial membrane and inner mitochondrial membrane.
